title: Epoch-based telemetry rehydration with checkpoint-aligned micro-batches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Console telemetry aggregates occasionally show gaps or double-counts when downstream consumers reingest historical events (late-arriving tokens, partition migrations, or partial pipeline restarts). Existing bulk reprocess jobs are heavy-weight, hard to resume cleanly, and cause spikes in ingestion lag and SLO violations. Goal: build a rehydration runner that applies historical events in checkpoint-aligned micro-batches (epochs) to make reprocessing resumable, idempotent, and cost-controlled while preserving analytic correctness and observability.

Scope: this ticket implements the core epoch-based runner, a compact resume token format, safety guards for duplicate detection, and a small canary pipeline. It does not include full UI controls in Console (follow-up).

Design summary:
- Epoch model: split historical time-range into N contiguous epochs (configurable epoch_duration_ms); each epoch corresponds to a compact micro-batch that can be scheduled, retried, or skipped.
- Checkpoint alignment: each epoch boundary is aligned to a source-partition checkpoint (Kafka offset or S3 manifest boundary) when available so we can achieve consistent, repeatable processing.
- Idempotency primitives: write operations to the downstream aggregate store use a two-part idempotency key: <epoch_id>|<entity_hash>. Aggregates updated with compare-and-swap on (entity_key, epoch_id) to ensure each event is applied at-most-once.
- Safe compaction pass: an optional compaction step can collapse intra-epoch duplicates before application using a deterministic reduction function to reduce write amplification.
- Resume tokens: compact JSON token per epoch shard with fields: epoch_id, source_boundary, applied_seq, checksum. Tokens are small and stored in the reprocessing state table; runner can resume from tokens and skip already-applied epochs.
- Resource control: runner limits concurrency per-source and throttles token consumption to maintain token-level latency SLOs for live traffic; supports a max-writes-per-second budget and backoff.
- Verification & invariants: after epoch application, runner computes a lightweight fingerprint of affected aggregates (e.g., CRC over rows touched) and compares against precomputed expected fingerprints for dry-run canaries.
- Observability: granular metrics: epoch_duration, epoch_apply_time_ms, epochs_applied, epochs_failed, resume_token_age, deduped_events, writes_per_second, estimated_cost_usd. Correlate logs to run-id and epoch-id.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Partial write: if an epoch fails mid-apply, resume token will reflect last fully-applied entity_seq and we retry the remainder. Use transactional apply per-entity where supported.
- Checkpoint mismatch: if source boundary metadata is missing or inconsistent, runner falls back to conservative epoch boundaries based on ingest timestamps and marks the epoch as 'best-effort' requiring manual review.
- High-cost spike: quota guard trips and cancels remaining epochs for that run, emits alert, and marks run for review.

Data safety & correctness trade-offs: we favor deterministic reductions and idempotent writes over attempting to reorder events for perfect causal fidelity. This keeps rehydration repeatable and auditable while avoiding unbounded complexity when ingest sources have non-monotonic timestamps.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Next steps: implement runner + state table + small canary that rehydrates the last 14 days for two low-volume customers, instrument metrics and a dry-run verifier, create runbook for ops, and schedule follow-up for Console UI controls.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can execute a full epoch-run over a 48h window split into <=96 epochs and produce resume tokens for each shard
Applying the same epoch-run twice does not change final aggregate values (idempotent) as validated by fingerprint comparison
Metrics emitted for epoch apply latency, deduped events, and resume token age are visible in Grafana dashboard 'analytics/rehydration'
Canary run against two low-volume orgs completes end-to-end without live-traffic SLO regressions (latency p95 increase < 5%)
Runbook and kill-switch documented with steps to pause, resume, or abort a run and to rebuild resume tokens from state table
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial design posted to Confluence; called out idempotency primitive and resume token format. Asked infra-team for feedback on state table schema.

2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (review): Suggest replacing compare-and-swap primitive with conditional upserts where the datastore supports it (Postgres ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with epoch check). Also flagged retention policy implications for resume tokens.

2026-03-04 - Luca Romero: Prototype runner implemented. Early observation: aligning to Kafka offsets requires reading partition metadata which adds 30-40ms per epoch boundary; added an optimization to reuse metadata cache across shards.

2026-03-05 - SRE (comment): Add circuit-breaker hook to the quota-guard to prevent a runaway run from exhausting write capacity in the aggregate cluster. Also requested metrics for resume_token_age and token_consumer_lag.

2026-03-07 - Aisha Patel: Updated ticket with canary plan and acceptance criteria. Created the PR for the state table schema and a prototype query for verification: SELECT count(*), crc32(string_agg(id||':'||value,',' ORDER BY id)) FROM aggregates WHERE updated_at BETWEEN $start AND $end;
